correctness.rationale: Burnside counting or complete rotation-class enumeration gives exactly 108 necklaces, partitioned into 56 even and 52 odd. Edges flip Hamming-weight parity, so a simple path can have at most 105 vertices. A direct standalone check of the 105 canonical rows finds no duplicates and verifies all 104 cyclic-Hamming-distance-one adjacencies, giving the matching lower bound. The proof is finite and exact; no solver trace or finite-sample extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The exact n=10 witness meets the preexisting bipartition upper bound and settles the first even order beyond the n<=8 cases recorded in the main 2016 paper and the 2019 thesis. Detailed inspection of the relevant full primary literature and recent survey, combined with searches for partial necklace Gray codes, parity saturation, and order-ten paths, found no statement or general construction implying this witness. The result is provisionally original, with explicit residual priority risk.
residual_risks: A separate published computation or an inaccessible thesis/table may have previously constructed a 105-vertex path for order ten.

value.rationale: The 2016 paper states explicit attainability as Conjecture 7.5 and verifies only even n≤8, so n=10 is the first subsequently motivated test case. Establishing the first unverified case with a compact explicit certificate is a meaningful finite cutoff of a natural Gray-code problem, even without a general theorem or downstream application. The 105 upper bound was known and is not itself represented as novel.
